title: fix(scripts): key the indirect registration bypass by collection, not by file
body:
Part of objectui#9717 — the mechanical half. ⚠️ Deliberately a `Part of`, never a closing keyword: the product question the card asks is still open, and a merge that quietly closed the card would take that question out of every open-issue sweep. This branch makes the question **visible and reviewable** instead of answering it.

Clause-②: no — no published surface moves. `scripts/` ships in no package's `files[]`, the derived key universe is byte-identical to the base commit (measured below, with its control), and `packages/cli/src/utils/known-schema-types.ts` is unchanged.

## What was wrong

`deriveRegistryKeys` waved a collection-keyed registration through — one whose key argument is not a string literal — whenever its **FILE** appeared in `INDIRECT_REGISTRATIONS`. That table's coverage is keyed by **COLLECTION**. The two keyings are not the same set, so **any** unresolvable registration living in a table-named file was skipped in silence, including one whose collection no entry names.

The card's instance: `registerAllFields()`'s `RETIRED_FIELD_TYPES` tombstone loop shares `packages/fields/src/index.tsx` with the `fieldWidgetMap` entry. Its keys reached neither the derived universe nor a finding — and its namespace was folded into the reconciliation of a collection it has nothing to do with.

## What changed

The supplying collection is **derived at the call** (`indirectSupply`) and matched against the entries declared for that file — the same treatment objectui#9703 gave the namespace, applied to the other half of the same entry. Two new reasons, parallel to that card's pair: `uncovered-indirect-collection` (the collection is readable and no entry names it) and `unresolved-indirect-collection` (the call cannot be paired with any collection — reading such a call as covered is the defect itself).

Per-collection keying also reaches the two readings that were file-keyed beside it: **namespace reconciliation** now reads the calls *that collection* feeds, and **staleness** is per collection, so a live sibling entry no longer answers for a dead one.

## What the alignment surfaced — and what each answer is

Two registrations, not the one the card knew about. Both are now declared; ⛔ neither is silenced.

**① `PALETTE_PLACEHOLDER_BLOCKS`** (`packages/components/src/renderers/placeholders.tsx`) — ordinary coverage. The same `registerPlaceholder` helper the declared `PROTOCOL_COMPONENTS` entry names is also handed this collection, eagerly, in every host. Declaring it adds **zero keys**, because its four members are today a subset of `PROTOCOL_COMPONENTS` — but that overlap is a coincidence nothing holds in place, and the next palette block that is not protocol vocabulary would have gone missing in exactly the same silence.

**② `RETIRED_FIELD_TYPES`** — **WITHHELD**, a new `excluded` disposition. It contributes no keys, names this card, and says in one line what deciding it either way would change. Today's behaviour is unchanged byte for byte — `field:owner` stays out of the universe, so a document teaching it stays red — **but now by declaration rather than by accident**. ⭐ The decision is still yours and it is now one line: drop the `excluded` line and the collection's keys enter the universe.

A withheld entry is not a quiet one. It is still reconciled against the call, it still reports `stale-indirect-registration` the moment the tombstone loop stops existing, and the gate's run summary prints `1 collection(s) declared and WITHHELD` on every run — an exclusion nobody can see from the gate's own output is a silence with extra steps.

## ⭐ The same mismatch, a third time — one gate over

A second entry on one `site` is what this diff makes possible, and it broke a sibling gate's arithmetic. `check-registry-bare-name-collisions.mjs` attributes a derived key by `entry.site` while coverage is now keyed by collection, so `at`, `names`, `bare` and the guard are a function of the file and the namespace and of nothing else in the entry — and iterating entries pushed the **same claim once per entry**. Its pass is now keyed the way its attribution is: one pass per `(site, namespace)`.

⛔ Those duplicates are not extra claims to deduplicate downstream. They are one claim counted twice, and that gate's verdict *is* a count of distinct claimants: two claims where the tree has one reads as `agreed` — "two registrations, one owner" — when the truth is `sole`. ⚠️ Note what that means about the green: this defect never touched that gate's red path, so nothing would have reported it. It was found by measuring, not by running.

## Measurements

**The universe does not move.** Base `4cf57b6da` and this branch both derive **649 keys**; the sorted key lists `diff` clean (exit 0). **Lit control on the same comparison**: one key deleted from the head list makes that same `diff` report a difference (exit 1) ⇒ the clean result is a reading. Exact whole-token probes on the final list: `field:owner` **0**, lit control `field:user` **1**, absent control `field:zzznosuch` **0**, `nav:menu` **1**, `protocol-placeholder:nav:menu` **1**. `node scripts/regenerate-known-schema-types.mjs --check` prints `OK … matches the registry derivation`.

⚠️ **One printed counter does move, and it is not a key count.** The run summary's indirect figure reads **132 → 136**. That counter counts collection MEMBER NAMES read through the table, not distinct keys — the four `PALETTE_PLACEHOLDER_BLOCKS` members are also `PROTOCOL_COMPONENTS` members, so they are counted twice and published once. The key count stays 649, which is the number that decides anything.

**The sibling gate's arithmetic is restored, and the restoration is measured by ablation.** With the dedupe removed on disk (blob `eac78264b` to `622f67c01`, `-48` bytes, anchor `claimedByNamespace` 3 occurrences to 2), the same instrument reads:

| reading | with the dedupe | ablated | base commit |
|---|---|---|---|
| registration claims | **425** | 554 | **425** |
| from declared collections | **129** | 258 | **129** |
| `sole` bare keys | **206** | 177 | **206** |
| `agreed` bare keys | **30** | 59 | **30** |
| `contested` / `declined` | **1 / 111** | 1 / 111 | **1 / 111** |

⇒ exactly **29** keys flip `sole` → `agreed` without the dedupe and exactly 29 flip back with it, matching the pre-emptive measurement; `contested` and `declined` cannot move and did not, which is the negative control on the same instrument. Both directions are pinned: the case that must collapse, and — ⭐ because a `(site, namespace)` dedupe would otherwise be a weakening wearing a bug fix's clothes — the case that must **survive**, two entries on one site under two different namespaces, which stays green under the ablation that reds the other.

**Ablation of the derivation itself.** Reverted to its base blob (`e4894c90c` to `c334f4730`, `-11214` bytes, anchor `indirectSupply` 5 occurrences to 0): exactly the four defect pins go red, both control pins stay green, and the live-tree assertion flips to GREEN — the surfacing shown failing in the only direction it can. Separately, ablating the `excluded` recognition alone (anchor `entry.excluded` 1 occurrence to 0) reds the WITHHELD coverage pin and returns the gate to `1 problem(s)` with `0 collection(s) declared and WITHHELD` in the summary. ⚠️ Stated exactly: of the three WITHHELD pins, **one** ablates; the other two assert properties that hold in both states (an excluded entry is still stale-checked, still reconciled) and are controls, not defect pins. Every mutation was proven on disk before any result was read, restored under a `trap` with an absolute path, and the restoration proven by blob equality with HEAD and an empty `git diff HEAD` — never by an exit code. ⚠️ One figure is NOT MEASURED: the byte delta of the `excluded` ablation, because the size was read with `git cat-file` against a blob that was never written to the object store; the hash change and the anchor count carry that leg instead.

## Gates — each exit code captured to disk before any pipe

| run | exit | printed verdict |
|---|---|---|
| `pnpm check:doc-types` | 0 | `✅ Every documented component type is registered.` — 649 keys, 136 indirect, 2 open, 1 withheld |
| `pnpm check:registry-bare-names` | 0 | `✓ no new bare-name collision` — 425 claims (129 from declared collections), 1 contested, ledger holds 1 |
| `pnpm check:prompt-keys` | 0 | `OK Every key taught as available is answered by a real renderer` — 535 authorable of 649 |
| `pnpm check:new-line-citations` | 0 | the `path:line` strings this adds are runtime-COMPUTED diagnostics |
| `node scripts/check-control-bytes.mjs` | 0 | `OK (scanned 7818 tracked text file(s))` — plus a direct scan of every changed file |
| `node scripts/check-changeset-presence.mjs` | 0 | nothing published moves |
| `node scripts/check-governed-queue-guard.mjs --test` | 0 | `NOT GOVERNED — 4 path(s) checked against 5 governed surface(s)` |
| `node scripts/regenerate-known-schema-types.mjs --check` | 0 | `OK … matches the registry derivation` |
| `pnpm exec vitest run scripts/` | 0 | `170 passed \| 2 skipped`, **4972 tests passed, 0 failed** |

⭐ That last run is the one that matters for the five red rows this branch carried at `3ecbe63669`: seven assertion sites in five files were failing on the same two findings, and all seven are green together now — verified by running them, not inferred from the two findings clearing.
